channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: Broomfield Hospital gets £4.3m nuclear medicine suite for cancer scans
item.description: Two new scanners at the Chelmsford hospital will help doctors find and track cancer, Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust says.

item.title: Essex weekend travel: buses replace trains from Colchester on Sunday
item.description: Rail passengers on the main line and the Braintree branch face replacement buses, and the QEII Bridge at the Dartford Crossing shuts overnight on Saturday 21 November.

item.title: Essex opticians treat new eye problems without a GP visit, NHS Essex says
item.description: The free Minor Eye Conditions Service runs at participating opticians across the county and can save patients a trip to A&E.

item.title: Maldon's Promenade Park gets free outdoor gym as work begins
item.description: Maldon District Council said on Friday 20 November that building has started on a new outdoor gym at Promenade Park in Maldon, free for visitors to use.

item.title: Essex anti-social behaviour reports up 76% as robbery falls 19%
item.description: The Seax analysis of police.uk data shows anti-social behaviour reports rose in 50 of Essex Police's 56 neighbourhood areas in September 2026 compared with September 2025, with Basildon recording the most.

item.title: Tendring offers £100,000+ in health grants to sport and community groups
item.description: Clubs and groups across the Tendring district can bid for money for projects that get people active, eating well or looking after their mental health.

item.title: NHS Essex looks for new online consultation tools for 204 GP surgeries
item.description: Suppliers can show their systems at an online event on 9 December, and a two-year contract is due to start in spring 2027.

item.title: Two taken to hospital after A282 crash shuts QEII Bridge for hours
item.description: Both were taken by road to the Royal London Hospital, and more closures are planned at the Dartford Crossing tonight and on Saturday.

item.title: Three Colchester food outlets hold hygiene ratings of 0 or 1
item.description: A High Street restaurant has the lowest rating, zero, and two other city centre businesses are rated one after inspections in October, an analysis of Food Standards Agency data by The Seax shows.

item.title: Grays school trust plans indoor padel courts on Green Belt site
item.description: South West Essex Community Education Trust wants to build a sports hall with two padel courts at William Edwards School in Grays, open to public bookings in the evenings.

item.title: Thurrock Council's Inspire careers team up for national inclusion award
item.description: Thurrock Council's Inspire Employability and Skills team is shortlisted for Inclusive Team of the Year at the Inspiring Women in Local Government Awards 2026.

item.title: Colchester Castle roof repairs finished after £1.3m project
item.description: Colchester City Council says work to stop water getting into the Norman keep has been completed.

item.title: 19-year-old Harlow man charged over hospital & McDonald's trespass
item.description: A Harlow man has been charged with entering a staff room at the town's hospital and an area of a McDonald's restaurant as a trespasser with intent to steal, Your Harlow reports.

item.title: Clacton Hospital's £25m revamp brings new urgent care centre
item.description: Children's services and musculoskeletal therapy have also moved into the rebuilt space, with Tendring council paying £2m of the cost.

item.title: Stansted Airport plans major emergency exercise with 400 taking part
item.description: London Stansted will rehearse its response to an aircraft accident using a decommissioned plane, and the airport says flights should not be affected.

item.title: Harlow's Avant Garde salon on The Rows shuts without warning
item.description: Clients of the long-running Harlow town centre hair and beauty salon found its doors shut this week.

item.title: Harlow to switch on bigger Christmas lights display on Broad Walk
item.description: Harlow Council says this year's town centre display is bigger and brighter than before, with lights across more of the town.

item.title: More than 10,000 expected for Southend's table-topping clash with Boreham Wood
item.description: Kieron Dyer is back on the touchline as third-placed Southend United try to become the first side to beat the National League leaders this season.

item.title: Basildon neighbour rescues sleeping woman after hearing smoke alarm
item.description: A woman who fell asleep while food was in the oven was helped out of her Basildon maisonette by a neighbour on 19 November.

item.title: Basildon councillors back permanent war memorial D-Day veteran sought
item.description: Basildon and Laindon have no permanent war memorial. Basildon Council has now voted unanimously to change that, taking up Don Sheppard's long campaign.

item.title: Colchester Hospital asks patients to hand back crutches and frames
item.description: The north Essex hospital trust cleans, checks and repairs returned walking aids so they can go to other patients.

item.title: Tendring plans to backdate council tax support for working-age claimants
item.description: Tendring District Council wants to extend a rule that now helps only pension-age claimants. Other council tax discounts and premiums in the district stay the same in 2027/28.

item.title: Tendring council runs £3.9m under budget at half-year, mainly on timing
item.description: Tendring District Council says the gap mainly reflects when money is spent and received across several budgets.

item.title: Maldon council to decide on 25-year River Blackwater foreshore leases
item.description: A boatyard business near Downs Road in Maldon uses two council-owned stretches of foreshore for access. Officers say it has a legal right to renew.

item.title: Abbotts Hall reserve near Colchester counts record number of rare moths
item.description: Essex Wildlife Trust has found more of a rare moth than ever before at its Abbotts Hall reserve after a conservation project there, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Grays scrapyard fire likely started by discarded battery, crews say
item.description: Essex County Fire and Rescue Service believes a thrown-away battery started the Little Thurrock scrapyard fire. About 20 firefighters had it out by 8.50pm on 19 November.

item.title: Harwich High Lighthouse to be lit for campaign against violence towards women
item.description: Harwich Town Council has fitted lighting equipment at the historic landmark and holds a Tendring District Council licence to light it up.

item.title: NHS Essex urges flu jabs by 11 December for Christmas protection
item.description: Anyone across Essex who is eligible for a free flu vaccine and has not yet had it should book now, because the jab takes up to two weeks to work, NHS Essex says.

item.title: Tilbury community pantry and café get go-ahead as works go to tender
item.description: An empty building next to Tilbury Library in Civic Square is to become a volunteer-run food pantry and café, months later than Thurrock Council first hoped.

item.title: Henham showhome wins national interior design award
item.description: A Bellway showhome in Henham, near Saffron Walden, has been named the best in the UK in a national interior design awards scheme.

item.title: Basildon firm AVRT trains soldiers and police in virtual reality
item.description: A three-person company in Basildon builds virtual reality training used by the British and Singaporean armies and trialled by UK police forces, The Standard reports.

item.title: Kelvedon's Monks Farm scheme of 600 homes wins planning approval
item.description: Braintree District Council has approved the housing development despite worries about traffic, infrastructure and the loss of countryside, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Thurrock road safety day reaches 200 Woodside School parents and pupils
item.description: A Road Safety Week day of education and enforcement in Thurrock saw the Safer Essex Roads Partnership talk to about 200 parents and children at Woodside School, with reflective ribbons handed out to pupils.

item.title: Uttlesford may charge for film ratings by length of the film
item.description: Uttlesford District Council is proposing new charges for classifying films, worked out on each film's running time.

item.title: A128 near Brentwood slowed by burst water main
item.description: Traffic was held up on the Brentwood road on Thursday 19 November while Essex and Suffolk Water repaired the burst main.

item.title: Burnham-on-Crouch swimmers cross Channel in relay for Havens Hospices
item.description: Five friends from Burnham-on-Crouch have raised more than £9,000 for Havens Hospices by swimming a relay from England to France through the night.

item.title: Colchester's Provide Community asked to pilot UK nursing public health framework
item.description: The Colchester-based community health provider has been invited to help test new guidance on how nurses, midwives and nursing associates prevent illness and tackle health inequalities.

item.title: c2c signalling fault near Barking disrupts trains on all routes
item.description: Passengers between Shoeburyness, Southend, Grays and London Fenchurch Street faced cancellations and delays of up to 20 minutes on the afternoon of Thursday 19 November.

item.title: Brightlingsea's Bayard Recreation Ground recovering after maintenance closure
item.description: Brightlingsea Town Council says the ground, shut since 16 October for maintenance, is gradually being restored and will reopen once the work is finished.

item.title: Clacton Victorian Christmas market raises more than £6,000 for charities
item.description: Tendring's biggest charity Christmas market filled Clacton Town Hall with 26 charity stalls, each keeping the money it took.

item.title: Pitsea man jailed over gunpowder as judge says ChatGPT fed his fears
item.description: The Pitsea man said he was getting ready to protect his family in a 'post-apocalyptic scenario'. He was sentenced at Basildon Crown Court for illegally having explosive powder.

item.title: Harlow hospital moves waiting list checks to My Alex Health app
item.description: Adults waiting for treatment at Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow will now get their 12-weekly waiting list questionnaire through the trust's own patient portal.

item.title: Colchester's Provide Community staff vote grants to 10 charities
item.description: Employee owners at Colchester-based Provide Community chose the causes, and the firm widened its October grants so all 10 shortlisted groups get money.

item.title: Shoeburyness picked for up to £20m from Pride in Place scheme
item.description: Shoeburyness is one of 399 wards in England chosen for Government money over 10 years through the Pride in Place scheme, SAVS Southend says.

item.title: Colchester city centre gets police knife arch checks
item.description: Essex Police set up a walk-through knife arch in Colchester city centre as part of its work against knife crime.

item.title: Writtle Green benches moved away from moth-hit oak
item.description: Writtle Parish Council has moved two benches from under a large oak on the Green that has been badly affected by oak processionary moth.

item.title: TG Jones to shut Harlow, Brentwood and Clacton shops
item.description: The former WH Smith high street chain plans to close its Harlow branch on 30 December and its Brentwood and Clacton branches on 12 January, ending their Post Office services, as the business is reviewed for sale.

item.title: Jaywick Sands' Brooklands could be rebuilt as one-way road with beach path
item.description: Tendring District Council has a preferred plan for the pothole-hit private road in Jaywick Sands, which residents named as their top priority for investment, but no decision has been taken.

item.title: Essex all-rounder Luc Benkenstein leaves for Durham
item.description: The leg-spinner has left by mutual agreement after 80 appearances across all formats since joining in 2021.

item.title: NHS Essex asks patients not to demand antibiotics for colds and flu
item.description: Across Essex, the county's NHS integrated care board says rising resistance is making some infections harder to treat, and wants people to take antibiotics only when prescribed and exactly as directed.

item.title: Essex Police arrest 17 in week-long county lines crackdown
item.description: Eleven people were charged and remanded, and officers seized 22 throwing blades, a zombie knife, drugs and cash.

item.title: Havens Hospices asks Essex schools to stage a Santa Run in December
item.description: Havens Hospices, which runs Little Havens children's hospice in Thundersley, wants schools to pick a December date for pupils to run, walk or skip in festive dress to raise sponsorship.

item.title: Harlow employment rate rises to 82.9% in latest ONS figures
item.description: Harlow is among the five best-performing areas in the country for jobs growth, according to Your Harlow's report on official labour market data.

item.title: University of Essex experts lead call for coastal focus in mental health plan
item.description: Close to 150 researchers, health leaders and charities have signed a letter, coordinated from the University of Essex in Colchester, warning that England's new Mental Health Strategy could overlook coastal, rural and former industrial communities.

item.title: Southend knife violence falls 23% but city still tops Essex list
item.description: Across Essex, serious violence involving knives has fallen 17% over two years, Essex Police says, while arrests for carrying knives rose 19% in the past 12 months.

item.title: Harlow's River Way Bridge to shut to all vehicles
item.description: The River Way Bridge in Harlow is to close fully to traffic, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Lakeside Retail Park to open King Living furniture showroom on Saturday
item.description: The family-owned Australian sofa and furniture maker is opening a two-floor store at West Thurrock, aimed at shoppers across Essex and east London.

item.title: Braintree MP Cleverly targets Khan on crime and housing in mayor bid
item.description: Sir James Cleverly took 86% of London Conservative members' votes on 19 November. Braintree's Conservatives must now find a new parliamentary candidate.

item.title: Southend homelessness charity HARP launches Christmas Unwrapped appeal
item.description: HARP is asking people and businesses in Southend and south Essex to give towards festive meals, gifts and treats for people experiencing homelessness this Christmas.

item.title: Stansted owner's survey puts east ahead for export growth
item.description: Six in 10 exporters in the East of England, which includes Essex, grew overseas sales between July and September, the best of four regions in a survey commissioned by London Stansted's owner MAG.
